arxiv-2011-14060.title: Unsupervised Spoken Term Discovery on Untranscribed Speech
arxiv-2011-14060.creator: SUNG, Man Ling
arxiv-2011-14060.description: Abstract Abstract Speech technology is becoming mature recent years mostly contributed to the development of deep neural network (DNN). However, under the situation when 1) there are not enough training data, and 2) phonetic information is absent, traditional acoustic modelling technique is no longer applicable.

arxiv-2110-14437.title: Exploring single-song autoencoding schemes for audio-based music structure analysis
arxiv-2110-14437.creator: Axel Marmoret, Jérémy E. Cohen \sthanks This work is partly supported by ANR JCJC project LoRAiA ANR-20-CE23-0010, Frédéric Bimbot
arxiv-2110-14437.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Axel Marmoret, Jérémy E. Cohen \sthanks This work is partly supported by ANR JCJC project LoRAiA ANR-20-CE23-0010, Frédéric Bimbot. The ability of deep neural networks to learn complex data relations and representations is established nowadays, but it generally relies on large sets of training data. This work explores a “piece-specific” autoencoding scheme, in which a low-dimensional autoencoder is trained to learn a latent/compressed representation specific to a given song, which can then be used to infer the song structure.

arxiv-2212-03854.title: BiPMAP: A Toolbox for Predicting Perceived Motion Artifacts on Modern Displays
arxiv-2212-03854.creator: Guanghan Meng*, Dekel Galor*, Laura Waller, and Martin S. Banks
arxiv-2212-03854.description: Abstract Viewers of digital displays often experience motion artifacts (e.g., flicker, judder, edge banding, motion blur, color breakup, depth distortion) when presented with dynamic scenes. We developed an interactive software tool for display designers that predicts how a viewer perceives motion artifacts for a variety of situations. We call it the Binocular Perceived Motion Artifact Predictor (BiPMAP).

arxiv-2402-02474.title: Deep Spectral Improvement for Unsupervised Image Instance Segmentation
arxiv-2402-02474.creator: Farnoosh Arefi, Amir M. Mansourian, Shohreh Kasaei
arxiv-2402-02474.description: Abstract Recently, there has been growing interest in deep spectral methods for image localization and segmentation, influenced by traditional spectral segmentation approaches. These methods reframe the image decomposition process as a graph partitioning task by extracting features using self-supervised learning and utilizing the Laplacian of the affinity matrix to obtain eigensegments.

arxiv-2408-09235.title: Reference-Guided Verdict: LLMs-as-Judges in Automatic Evaluation of Free-Form QA
arxiv-2408-09235.creator: Sher Badshah, Hassan Sajjad
arxiv-2408-09235.description: Abstract The emergence of Large Language Models (LLMs) as chat assistants capable of generating human-like conversations has amplified the need for robust evaluation methods, particularly for open-ended tasks. Conventional metrics such as EM and F1, while useful, are inadequate for capturing the full semantics and contextual depth of such generative outputs.

arxiv-2411-17836.title: The zero entropy locus for the Lozi maps Thanks: S.Š. is supported in part by the Croatian Science Foundation grant IP-2022-10-9820 GLODS
arxiv-2411-17836.creator: M. Misiurewicz and S. Štimac
arxiv-2411-17836.description: Abstract . We study the zero entropy locus for the Lozi maps. We first define a region R R in the parameter space and prove that for the parameters in R R , the Lozi maps have the topological entropy zero.

arxiv-2503-10064.title: Capturing an Electron in the Virtual State
arxiv-2503-10064.creator: Alok Nath Singh, Bibek Bhandari, Rafael Sánchez, Andrew N. Jordan
arxiv-2503-10064.description: Abstract We address a foundational question in quantum mechanics: can a particle be directly found in a classically forbidden virtual state? We instantiate this conceptual question by investigating the traversal of electrons through a tunnel barrier, which we define in a triple quantum dot (TQD) system where the occupation of the central dot is energetically avoided.

arxiv-2508-02604.title: Periodic robust robotic rock chop via virtual model control
arxiv-2508-02604.creator: Yi Zhang, Fumiya Iida, Fulvio Forni
arxiv-2508-02604.description: Abstract Robotic cutting is a challenging contact-rich manipulation task where the robot must simultaneously negotiate unknown object mechanics, large contact forces, and precise motion requirements. We introduce a new virtual-model control scheme that enables knife rocking motion for robot manipulators, without pre-planned trajectories or precise information of the environment.

arxiv-2601-13811.title: Quantum simulation of general spin-1/2 Hamiltonians with parity-violating fermionic Gaussian states
arxiv-2601-13811.creator: Michael Kaicher, Joseph Vovrosh, Alexandre Dauphin, Simon B. Jäger
arxiv-2601-13811.description: Abstract We introduce equations of motion for a parity-violating fermionic mean-field theory (PV-FMFT): a numerically efficient fermionic mean-field theory based on parity-violating fermionic Gaussian states (PV-FGS). This work provides explicit equations of motion for studying the real- and imaginary-time evolution of spin-1/2 Hamiltonians with arbitrary geometries and interactions.

pmc-10644861.title: Identification and verification of ferroptosis-related genes in the pathology of epilepsy: insights from CIBERSORT algorithm analysis
pmc-10644861.creator: Dan Xu, ManMan Chu, YaoYao Chen, Yang Fang, JingGuang Wang, XiaoLi Zhang, FaLin Xu
pmc-10644861.description: BackgroundEpilepsy is a neurological disorder characterized by recurrent seizures. A mechanism of cell death regulation, known as ferroptosis, which involves iron-dependent lipid peroxidation, has been implicated in various diseases, including epilepsy.ObjectiveThis study aimed to provide a comprehensive understanding of the relationship between ferroptosis and epilepsy through bioinformatics analysis.

pmc-10752810.title: An Overview of the Role of Peroxisome Proliferator-activated Receptors in Liver Diseases
pmc-10752810.creator: Zahra Changizi, Forough Kajbaf, Azam Moslehi
pmc-10752810.description: Peroxisome proliferator-activated receptors (PPARs) are a superfamily of nuclear transcription receptors, consisting of PPARα, PPARγ, and PPARβ/δ, which are highly expressed in the liver. They control and modulate the expression of a large number of genes involved in metabolism and energy homeostasis, oxidative stress, inflammation, and even apoptosis in the liver.

pmc-11674711.title: Vitamin E Mitigates Apoptosis in Ovarian Granulosa Cells by Inhibiting Zearalenone-Induced Activation of the PERK/eIF-2α/ATF4/Chop Signaling Pathway
pmc-11674711.creator: Qingxiu Liu, Leli Wang, Lei An, Yafei Liu, Honglei Qu, Shimeng Huang, Lihong Zhao, Yulong Yin, Qiugang Ma
pmc-11674711.description: A study aimed to investigate the signaling pathway of zearalenone (ZEA) leading to the apoptosis of ovarian granulosa cells (GCs) and explore the potential of vitamin E (VE) in alleviating ZEA-induced apoptosis of GCs. We constructed an apoptosis model for GCs based on exposure to the environmental toxin ZEA.

pmc-12532401.title: The critical role of diagnostic accuracy in differentiating uterine dehiscence and placenta accreta spectrum to enhance neonatal outcomes in complex cesarean sections
pmc-12532401.creator: Kartika Darma Handayani, Avianita Dewi Kusumawardhani, Anang Endaryanto, Lavenia Kurniawati, Gondo Mastutik, Dina Angelika, Risa Etika, Martono Tri Utomo, Pieter J.J. Sauer, Rozi Aditya Aryananda
pmc-12532401.description: AimThis study aims to analyze the key factors that contribute to adverse neonatal outcomes in complex cesarean sections with a high risk of placenta accreta spectrum (PAS).MethodsA retrospective analysis was conducted on 454 records collected between January 2018 and December 2023 at a single tertiary hospital, Dr. Soetomo General Hospital, Surabaya, East Java. The PAS diagnosis was confirmed intraoperatively.

pmc-12571743.title: Lactylation and antitumor immunity
pmc-12571743.creator: Biao Yang, Lingyu Li, Dongmei Shi, Tao Zhong, Huabao Xiong
pmc-12571743.description: Lactylation, a recently discovered post-translational modification (PTM), plays a critical role in cancer biology. Warburg effect induces lactate accumulation, which serves as a metabolic end-product and intercellular signaling mediator within the tumor microenvironment (TME). Beyond fueling tumor growth, elevated lactate levels drive histone and non-histone lactylation, which modulates gene expression and protein function.

pmc-12650677.title: Genetic Diversity of Sweetpotato (Ipomoea batatas (L.) Lam.) from Portugal, Mozambique and Timor-Leste
pmc-12650677.creator: Joana B Guimarães, Maria Cristina Simões-Costa, Milton Pinho, Celina Maria Godinho, Paula Sá Pereira, João Neves Martins, Ana Ribeiro-Barros, Pedro Talhinhas, Maria Manuela Veloso, Qiang Li
pmc-12650677.description: Simple SummaryHistorically, Portugal played a role in the global diffusion of sweetpotato (Ipomoea batatas). Although, at present, the crop holds limited importance on the Portuguese mainland, it is still highly relevant in the Azores and Madeira archipelagos and in the Portuguese ex-colonies Mozambique and Timor-Leste.

pmc-12821886.title: Treatment guided by cerebral oximetry in mechanically ventilated newborns: a statistical analysis plan for step one of the SafeBoosC-IIIv randomised clinical trial
pmc-12821886.creator: Johanne Juul Petersen, Caroline Barkholt Kamp, Markus Harboe Olsen, Mathias Lühr Hansen, Kristian Thorlund, Adelina Pellicer, Gunnar Naulaers, Eugene Dempsey, Gitte Holst Hahn, Patrick Bjerregaard Andersen, Marie Isabel Skov Rasmussen, Gerhard Pichler, Gabriel Dimitriou, Tomasz Szczapa, Maria Livia
pmc-12821886.description: BackgroundNewborns requiring invasive mechanical ventilation are at high risk of neurodevelopmental impairment, prolonged hospitalisation, and increased mortality. Treatment guided by cerebral oximetry monitoring has been proposed to reduce morbidity and mortality.MethodsThe SafeBoosC-IIIv trial is a multicentre, parallel-group, randomised clinical trial. The trial will be conducted in two steps. This is a statistical analysis plan for step one.

pmc-13236096.title: Immune checkpoint inhibitor–related eruptive keratoacanthoma
pmc-13236096.creator: Kazuki Watanabe, Mitsuhito Ota
pmc-13236096.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). We identified discrete erythematous hard papules of up to 8 mm in diameter on the patient’s forearms and dorsal hands (Figure 1A). Some papules showed crateriform appearances with hyperkeratosis (Figure 1B). He had no oral mucosal lesions. We performed a skin biopsy, which showed a keratin-filled crater and irregular epidermal proliferations with mild atypical keratinocytes (Appendix 1, available at www.cmaj.ca/lookup/doi/10.1503/cmaj.252150/tab-related-content). We diagnosed eruptive keratoacanthoma attributed to pembrolizumab. We treated the patient with cryotherapy and topical corticosteroids, with complete resolution within 2 months.

pmc-13331731.title: A community-engaged investigation of residential polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon exposures in West Eugene, OR
pmc-13331731.creator: Francesca Germano, Lane G Tidwell, Duo Jiang, Arjorie Arberry-Baribeault, Lisa Arkin, Michael Barton, Kim A Anderson, Diana Rohlman
pmc-13331731.description: BackgroundA West Eugene, OR community has a history of odor complaints, anecdotally linked to a nearby wood preservative facility using creosote, a known source of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs). The community also experiences elevated cancer risks.ObjectiveIn response to concerns about industrial air pollution, Beyond Toxics (BT) and Oregon State University (OSU) initiated a community-engaged study to characterize residential PAH exposure.Methods.

pmc-13657813.title: Multi-cohort validation of BRAF-PTPRT co-mutation as a predictor of favorable immunotherapy response in melanoma
pmc-13657813.creator: Dongmei Han, Caihong Wu, Dan Wang, Hao Jin, Weishuai Liu
pmc-13657813.description: BackgroundImmune checkpoint blockade (ICB) has transformed melanoma therapy, but predictive biomarkers remain suboptimal. BRAF is the most common driver mutation, yet its single-gene association with ICB response remains inconsistent. PTPRT loss activates STAT3-driven immunity. We hypothesized that concurrent BRAF and PTPRT mutations (co-mutation) synergistically enhance immunogenicity and predict ICB benefit.

uslaw-usc-t10-s14006.title: 10 U.S.C. § 14006 — Determination of years in grade
uslaw-usc-t10-s14006.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t10-s14006.description: United States Code, Title 10 (Armed Forces); Part III (Promotion And Retention Of Officers On The Reserve Active-Status List); Chapter 1401 (Applicability And Reserve Active-Status Lists). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. For the purpose of chapters 1403 through 1411 of this title, an officer’s years of service in a grade are computed from the officer’s date of rank in grade as determined.
